High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:182240
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 10468 of 2023
Applicant :- Manmohan Singh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Omar Zamin

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant - Manmohan Singh seeking
anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 214 of 2022, under Sections 409, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 Ipc,
Police Station Kotwali, District Azamgarh.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.

It is further submitted that the applicant was never posted as Clerk in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.11,
Azamgarh.

entities.text:
Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.11,
Azamgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that no fine deposit receipt has been issued by the applicant, as alleged in the F.I.R..

It is further submitted that as a matter of fact he was transferred to the Court of Additional Civil Judge (J.D.), Court No.20, Azamgarh on 04.10.2020 and since he found several anomalies in the said office, he immediately informed the facts to the District Judge through his Presiding Officer.

entities.text: Court of Additional Civil Judge (J.D.), Court No.20, Azamgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that the booklet containing receipt nos. 0472701 to 0472750 is Manmohan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127712607/
1 still kept safe with the applicant, which was issued to him by the library and the said booklet is intact as yet and no receipt has been issued from the aforesaid booklet.

entities.text: Manmohan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said fact was also brought to the knowledge of the District Judge concerned by his letter dated 17.5.2022 with the annexure of relevant receipts.

It is further submitted that during the departmental enquiry since F.I.R. was lodged against the applicant, he was not in a position to put forth his defence before the Inquiry Officer and that is why the enquiry was culminated against him.

It is also submitted that earlier the applicant was granted anticipatory bail by this Court on 13.4.2023 vide Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 CrPC No. 1041 of 2023 till the submission of police report under Section 173(2) CrPC and the said liberty has not been misused by him.

After completion of investigation,
charge sheet has been submitted in the matter.
No process under Sections 82 and 83 CrPC has been issued against the applicant and the applicant has not been declared absconder.
It is also submitted that without any cogent and sufficient evidence, charge sheet has been submitted in haste against the applicant by the Investigating Officer.
Applicant has no criminal history to his credit.
In case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
5. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

6. The prosecution story, as unfolded in the F.I.R., is that some fine receipts having forged signature and seal of the Presiding Officer / Court were procured by the present applicant, who was working as Senior Clerk in the Civil Court, Azamgarh and whose name came into light after enquiry.

F.I.R.
was lodged by the informant, clerk of A.C.J.M., Court No.11, Azamgarh on 19.5.2022 and after investigation, charge sheet has been submitted.

It also reveals from the perusal of the record that the applicant was never posted in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.11,
Azamgarh rather he was a clerk in the Court of Additional Civil Judge (JD)/ Judicial Magistrate,
Court No.20, Azamgarh and the booklet containing the relevant receipts is kept intact with the applicant.

sentences.text: It further reveals from the perusal of the case diary that the Advocate, who allegedly named the present applicant, was never interrogated by the Investigating Officer and it appears that the Investigating Officer has also made no effort to assure this fact that the police personnel who made a conversation with the applicant at the instance of the Advocate on phone, was the applicant himself or any other person.

7. Although charge sheet has been submitted in the present matter, but in Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled the law on the subject finally by holding that the anticipatory bail need not be of limited duration invariably.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appropriate case, it can continue upto conclusion of trial.
It has been further held therein that anticipatory bail granted can, depending on the conduct and behavior of the accused, continue after filing of the charge sheet till end of trial.

It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the Manmohan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127712607/
2 likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, likelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

entities.text: Manmohan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

8. Considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, in my view, it is a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant till the end of trial.
9. The application is allowed accordingly.

10. In the event of arrest of the applicant, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make himself available before the Court concerned on the date fixed in the matter and will cooperate in the trial.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office.

(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
Concerned.
11. In case of default of any of the conditions, the same may be a ground for cancellation of protection granted to the applicant.
